QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_37

question.text: Hariyali Foundation planted 50,000 saplings and claims 70% 3-year survival. Control sites show 30% natural regrowth. Under SAS-500, the NET ADDITIONAL impact (net trees attributable to the SE) is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Net additional = Gross surviving − Deadweight (what would have happened anyway). 50,000 × 70% survival = 35,000 gross. Deadweight 30% means 15,000 would have regrown naturally. Net = 35,000 − 15,000 = 20,000 additional trees. This is the standard SAS-500 attribution calculation. The Trap: Option B ignores deadweight. Option C is gross planted (not survived). Option D misapplies the formula. Cross-Exam Context: Counterfactual / deadweight logic aligned with carbon-accounting additionality (VCS, Gold Standard) and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — impact attribution). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always confirm the control-site selection process — if the SE picks the control, there is selection bias. Push for random selection of control sites or use a published regrowth rate from the same eco-zone.
